title: Inline error messages are silent to assistive tech (no role=alert/aria-live, no aria-describedby)
description:
Several async form-submission error paths render a plain styled
//

, so a screen-reader user who activates the control hears nothing and must hunt the page to discover the failure. Locations: MapExplorer.tsx:105 (place-name search failure), :687 (geolocation error), :1006-1011 (Find Hotspots error), :1227-1232 (Find Recent Sightings error); Settings.tsx:300-309 (malformed/failed CSV upload error in FileRow), :476-485 (API-key save error in KeyRow), :1210 (map-location detect error), :1281-1283 (map defaults save error — additionally the text 'Check your values and try again.' does not identify which of the three fields is invalid); ListComparer.tsx:276-280 (my-list load error). None are associated to their input via aria-describedby either. The codebase has correct reference implementations: App.tsx:668+717-736 (role=alert plus aria-describedby on the input), ChecklistComparer.tsx:372, DropZone.tsx:132, WeatherTidePanel.tsx:184.
fix: Give each error container role="alert" (or aria-live="polite" for non-urgent ones), and where the error relates to a specific input add id + aria-describedby on that input (the App.tsx checklist-input pattern). Make the map-defaults message name the offending field, e.g. "Latitude must be between -90 and 90."

verdict.reasoning: Every cited location verified as a plain styled div/span/p (MapExplorer 105/687/1006/1227, Settings 300-309/476-485/1210/1281-1283 including the field-anonymous 'Check your values' message, ListComparer 276-280); grep shows zero role=alert or aria-live in those files. The cited correct reference implementations all exist (App.tsx role=alert + aria-describedby, ChecklistComparer 372, DropZone 132, WeatherTidePanel 184), so this is inconsistent application of an established house pattern. Serious is fair for 4.1.3/3.3.1: async failures on key flows (location search, CSV upload, API-key save) are completely silent to SR users.

title: Footer update-checker outcomes auto-dismiss on fixed 4–8s timers with no way to extend — including the web path's actionable 'update available' instruction
description: Every outcome of the user-initiated 'Check For Updates' action is erased by a content-set time limit with no mechanism to turn off, adjust, or extend it (none of the 2.2.1 exceptions — real-time, essential, 20-hour — applies). Worst case: on the WEB path, the 'available' state renders 'v{latest} available — run ./update.sh' (App.tsx:1172-1177) — actionable content the user must read, remember, and carry to a terminal — and auto-reverts to idle after 8000ms (App.tsx:505). The Tauri path proves persistence is the intended design: its 'available' state (App.tsx:492-493) has NO timer and keeps its Install button indefinitely, so the web timer is an arbitrary asymmetry. Additionally, 'up-to-date' ('Up to date (v{current})' — the answer to the user's question, shown nowhere else) and 'error' ('Could not check for updates') auto-revert after 4000ms (App.tsx:491, 496, 502, 510; the post-install failure at 524), after which the footer returns to the bare 'Check For Updates' button — indistinguishable from never having clicked. A screen-magnifier user panning the viewport, a user reading at 200% text size, or a user with a cognitive disability can entirely miss a 4-second message, and because the timer re-arms on every check, re-clicking the button is not an extension mechanism — the reading window can never exceed 8 seconds. This compounds verified finding i=35 (the 'available' and 'error' states are also never announced to AT): for a screen-reader user the error outcome is both silent AND gone within 4 seconds. Applying the brief-success-confirmation reasoning explicitly: only 'up-to-date' resembles a success confirmation, and even it carries content (the version number) with no persistent equivalent; 'available' and 'error' are informational/actionable outcomes, not confirmations, so the commonly-accepted toast exemption does not cover them.
evidence: App.tsx:505 `updateTimerRef.current = setTimeout(() => setUpdateStatus({ kind: 'idle' }), 8000)` on the web 'available' branch, whose render (App.tsx:1173-1175) is 'v{updateStatus.latest} available — run ./update.sh'; the Tauri 'available' branch at 492-493 sets state with no timer; 'up-to-date'/'error' timers at 491, 496, 502, 510, 524 all revert to {kind:'idle'} after 4000ms, unmounting the message span (renders at 1153-1154, 1190-1192).
suggestedFix: Remove the auto-revert timers for the 'available' (web) and 'error' states — let them persist until the user acts, exactly as the Tauri 'available' state already does (render the 'Check For Updates' button alongside or convert the message to include a dismiss/recheck affordance). For 'up-to-date', either let it persist with the recheck button returning next to it, or keep an auto-revert only if the duration is generous (20s+) — though persisting is simpler and costs nothing in a footer. This pairs naturally with the fix for verified finding i=35: one persistent aria-live span whose text changes per state, with the timer logic deleted rather than announced.

verdict.reasoning: All six timers verified at App.tsx:491/496/502/510/524 (4000ms) and :505 (8000ms on the web 'available' branch, whose render at 1173-1176 contains the actionable './update.sh' instruction); the Tauri 'available' branch (492-493) persists indefinitely, proving the asymmetry. No 2.2.1 exception applies and re-clicking is not an Extend mechanism (each window stays ≤8s, no warning, <20s); the 'up-to-date' answer and the error message vanish in 4s leaving the footer indistinguishable from never having clicked. Distinct root cause (content-set time limits, 2.2.1) from confirmed i=35 (live-region semantics, 4.1.3) and absent from both findings files, so not a duplicate; moderate is fair given it compounds i=35 on the same user-initiated flow.
verdict.fixNote: Delete the timers for 'available' (web) and 'error' and let them persist like the Tauri 'available' branch; re-render the 'Check For Updates' button alongside the persistent message (also resolving the idle-button unmount focus drop noted under i=28). Fold into i=35's fix: one always-mounted aria-live span whose text changes per state, timer logic removed rather than announced.

title: No h1, most views have no headings, and heading levels are inconsistent across tabs
description: The app title "SnowRaven" is styled <span>s in a <div> (App.tsx:570-580) — no h1 and no banner landmark. Settings, Life List, Species Detail, and Map Explorer contain no heading elements at all (section titles like "Appearance"/"Map Overlays" are styled divs), so SR heading navigation lands on nothing in four major views. Where headings do exist they are inconsistent: ListComparer.tsx:184 and ChecklistComparer.tsx:340 use h1 inside tab content while Checklists.tsx:522, BirdingStats.tsx:424 and NamedBirds.tsx:128 use h2; SetupRequired.tsx:31 (the empty state of 8 tabs) styles its title as a div. Additionally the main nav loses its landmark: role="tablist" on the <nav> (TabNav.tsx:105-108) overrides the navigation role, and in dropdown mode there is no nav element at all.
fix: Make the app title an h1 inside a <header>; give every tab view an h2 and section cards h3 (Settings/LifeList/SpeciesDetail/MapExplorer sidebar sections); make SetupRequired's title an h2; demote the comparer h1s to h2.

verdict.reasoning: All claims check out: the title is styled spans in a div (App.tsx:570-580, no h1/header element); grep shows zero heading elements in Settings, LifeList, SpeciesDetail, MapExplorer and SetupRequired (title is a styled div, SetupRequired.tsx:31); ListComparer:184/ChecklistComparer:340 use h1 in tab content while Checklists:522/BirdingStats:424/NamedBirds:128 use h2; TabNav.tsx:105-108 puts role="tablist" on the <nav> (killing the navigation landmark) and the dropdown variant renders no nav at all. Heading navigation is a primary SR strategy and four major views expose nothing, so this is genuinely user-impacting at 1.3.1 Level A; moderate is the right tier since tablist/main/contentinfo landmarks still give a navigation path.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested heading plan is sound (h1 title in <header>, h2 per view incl. SetupRequired, h3 section cards — statsPrimitives.tsx already uses h3 for stats cards, so follow that pattern), but it omits the landmark half of its own description: also move role="tablist" off the <nav> in TabNav.tsx onto an inner div so the navigation landmark survives, and wrap the dropdown-mode trigger+listbox in the same <nav aria-label="Main navigation">.

title: Entire Weather tabpanel is an aria-live aria-atomic region
description: The whole weather panel carries aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true" (App.tsx:591-592). With aria-atomic, ANY mutation — the button flipping to "Looking up…", Copy → "Copied!", the tide box changing state — re-announces the entire panel content (label, help text, full weather <pre>, tide section). The nested role="alert" (:720) and role="status" elements (:837-845) inside the live region then announce the same changes a second time. Screen-reader users get long duplicate read-outs after every interaction on the default tab.
fix: Remove aria-live/aria-atomic from the tabpanel; rely on the existing scoped role="alert"/role="status" children, and add a small persistent polite region for "Weather copied to clipboard" if needed.

verdict.reasoning: App.tsx:587-592 carries aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true" on the entire weather tabpanel, with nested role="alert" (:720) and role="status" (:837-845) regions inside it — every state flip (Looking up…, Copied!, tide states, result insertion) re-announces the full panel atomically plus a duplicate from the scoped child region. This is the default tab, so the verbosity hits every screen-reader session; moderate is correct (annoyance/verbosity, not blocked function). ACCESSIBILITY.md describes the live region as a feature ('announced politely'), not as a known exception, so not disclosed. The suggested fix (drop the panel-level live attrs, keep the scoped children, add a small persistent polite region for the copy confirmation) is correct and matches the existing scoped role=status/alert pattern.

title: Map fullscreen overlay: no Escape exit and focus tabs into content obscured behind the overlay
wcag: 2.4.3 Focus Order A (also 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured Minimum, WCAG 2.2 AA)
description: Fullscreen turns the Map Explorer tabpanel into `position: fixed; inset: 0; zIndex: 1200` (App.tsx:1031-1034) with body scroll locked (App.tsx:390-395), but no keydown handler exits it (grep confirms no Escape handler in App.tsx; the only Escape handlers in the app are the sidebar trap, HelpDocs, the combobox, TabNav, WelcomeScreen). The page chrome (tab bar, footer links, other panels' controls) stays in the DOM and in the tab order BEHIND the overlay, so a keyboard user who tabs past the map's controls watches focus vanish under the map — the focus indicator is rendered but fully obscured. Exit is possible only by finding the Exit-fullscreen FAB again. Escape is the universally expected exit for a viewport-takeover, and the obscured-focus walk is disorienting.
fix: While mapFullscreen: add a document keydown listener that exits on Escape (returning focus to the fullscreen toggle), and apply `inert` to the app shell siblings (or trap Tab within the fullscreen panel) so focus cannot land behind the overlay.

verdict.reasoning: Fullscreen overlay styles (App.tsx:1031-1033) and body scroll lock (:390-395) exist exactly as cited; grep confirms no Escape handler or inert/focus-trap for fullscreen anywhere (MapExplorer.tsx:200's Escape handler is the mobile filters-panel trap only). The footer links/buttons and tab bar stay focusable behind the fixed z-1200 panel, so the obscured-focus walk is real; exit is FAB-only. Fairly flagged under 2.4.11 (WCAG 2.2 AA) with a real keyboard-UX gap; moderate is right since a keyboard exit does exist.
verdict.fixNote:
Put the Escape handling inside MapExplorer rather than App: MapExplorer owns onToggleFullscreen AND the sidebarOpen filters trap (MapExplorer.tsx:187-221), which already listens for Escape on document — an independent App-level listener would close the filters panel and exit fullscreen on the same keypress. Exit fullscreen on Escape only when sidebarOpen is false (innermost layer first), returning focus to the fullscreen FAB. For the obscured-focus half, React 19 (in use, ^19.2.5) supports the boolean inert prop — set inert on the header div, TabNav, footer

, and sibling tabpanels while mapFullscreen && activeTab === 'map-explorer'.

title: Update-check outcomes are not reliably announced ('available' and 'error' not at all)
description: The footer update checker swaps conditionally-rendered spans per state. 'checking' (:1148), 'up-to-date' (:1154) and 'downloading' (:1180) have aria-live="polite" but each span MOUNTS already containing its text — newly-inserted live regions with initial content are inconsistently announced by AT. The two states that matter most, 'available' (:1156-1178, with its Install update button) and 'error' (:1190), have no live semantics at all, so a screen-reader user who activates "Check For Updates" may hear nothing whatsoever.
fix: Render ONE persistent <span aria-live="polite"> in the footer and change its text content across all update states, instead of mounting/unmounting per-state spans.

verdict.reasoning: Verified all five state branches: 'checking' (:1148), 'up-to-date' (:1154), 'downloading' (:1180) mount aria-live spans already containing their text, and 'available' (:1156-1178) and 'error' (:1190) have no live semantics at all — a screen-reader user activating Check For Updates can hear nothing for the two outcomes that matter (the idle button also unmounts, so there's no visual-focus fallback either). Moderate is fair: explicit user action with potentially zero feedback, on a feature central to desktop updating. The suggested fix (one persistent always-mounted aria-live span whose text changes across states) is the standard correct pattern; keep the Install-update button as a sibling outside the live span so its mount doesn't depend on live-region timing.

title: Desktop updater: download progress has no progressbar semantics and mutates a polite live region on every network chunk; the flow ends in an unannounced self-restart ('ready-to-restart' is dead UI set after relaunch() has begun)
wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value A / 4.1.3 Status Messages AA (3.2.2 advisory)
description: Desktop-only updater states beyond verified-finding i=35's scope (which covered only the unreliable mount-with-text announcement of checking/up-to-date/downloading and the missing announcements for 'available'/'error' — not re-reported here): (1) No progressbar semantics: the 'downloading' state (App.tsx:1179-1186) conveys progress purely as text ("Downloading… N%") in an aria-live="polite" span, with no role="progressbar", aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin/max, or aria-busy — AT cannot query the operation's progress as a value. (2) Unthrottled live-region churn: handleInstallUpdate's callback (App.tsx:518-520) calls setUpdateStatus on EVERY 'Progress' chunk event from update.downloadAndInstall (lib/tauri/updateManager.ts:36-42), so the live region's text content mutates dozens-to-hundreds of times across a multi-megabyte universal-bundle download; polite regions queue each text change, so VoiceOver/NVDA either chatter stale percentages for the entire download or coalesce unpredictably. (3) The terminal state is imperceivable: updateManager.downloadAndInstall() awaits relaunch() — which terminates the process — BEFORE returning (updateManager.ts:49-50), so setUpdateStatus({kind:'ready-to-restart'}) at App.tsx:521 runs only as the process is already exiting; the "Update installed — restarting…" span (App.tsx:1187-1189) is statically dead UI, and even if it paints for a frame it carries no live semantics. The resulting SR experience: "Downloading… 97%", then the application silently quits and relaunches with no completion message and no prior notice — the trigger is labeled only "Install update" (App.tsx:1169), nothing warns of the immediate automatic restart. Additional note, NOT counted as a new finding: the 'idle' "Check For Updates" button (App.tsx:1129-1146) and the "Install update" button unmount on activation, dropping keyboard focus to <body> — two further locations of the unmount-on-activation pattern already recorded as verified-finding i=28, whose location list omits the footer. needs-runtime-verification: whether the 'ready-to-restart' frame ever paints before process exit, and the actual VoiceOver/NVDA behavior on the per-chunk live updates.
evidence: App.tsx:1180-1185 `<span aria-live="polite">…{updateStatus.progress !== null ? `Downloading… ${Math.round(updateStatus.progress * 100)}%` : 'Downloading update…'}` (no progressbar role); App.tsx:518-520 setUpdateStatus inside the per-chunk onProgress; updateManager.ts:36-43 onProgress fires per 'Progress' event, :49-50 `const { relaunch } = await import('@tauri-apps/plugin-process'); await relaunch();` before the function returns; App.tsx:1187-1189 plain span with no live attributes.
suggestedFix: Give the downloading indicator role="progressbar" with aria-valuemin={0} aria-valuemax={100} aria-valuenow={Math.round(progress*100)} (and aria-label="Downloading update"), and throttle state/announcement updates (e.g. update only when the rounded percent crosses a 5-10% step, or announce milestones at 25/50/75/100 via the single persistent polite live region that finding i=35 already recommends for the footer). Announce intent up front: on Install activation, push "Downloading update — SnowRaven will restart automatically when finished" into that live region, and/or rename the button "Install update and restart". If a perceivable completion state is wanted, split relaunch() out of downloadAndInstall(): set 'ready-to-restart', announce it assertively, then call relaunch() after a short delay.

verdict.reasoning: All three sub-claims verified in code: the 'downloading' span (App.tsx:1180-1185) is a text-only aria-live region with no progressbar role/values; setUpdateStatus fires on every 'Progress' chunk (App.tsx:518-520, updateManager.ts:36-42) so the polite region's text mutates per network chunk; and updateManager.ts:49-50 awaits relaunch() — which exits the process — before returning, making the 'ready-to-restart' state at App.tsx:521 and its non-live span (1187-1189) statically dead, so the app silently quits at ~100% with the trigger labeled only 'Install update'. Genuinely distinct from confirmed i=35 (announcement reliability of mounted spans, not value semantics, churn, or the restart) and from i=70 (keystroke churn at a different location); not in either findings file. Moderate is right: a screen-reader user gets chatter then an unexplained app disappearance on a desktop-critical flow.
verdict.fixNote: Fix is sound and convention-compatible: add role="progressbar" with aria-valuemin/max/now, throttle updates to ~5% steps, announce the impending automatic restart up front (or rename the button 'Install update and restart'), and optionally split relaunch() out of downloadAndInstall() so App can set/announce 'ready-to-restart' before relaunching — CLAUDE.md only requires relaunch() (not exit(0)) after downloadAndInstall returns, which this preserves. Route announcements through the single persistent live span from i=35's fix.

title: In-page jump links scroll the view but never move keyboard focus
description: The Statistics "Jump to section" nav (9 anchors) calls e.preventDefault() + smoothScrollIntoView, and LifeList's "media comments" anchor does the same (LifeList.tsx:505). preventDefault suppresses the browser's native sequential-focus relocation for fragment navigation, and the scroll targets are plain divs without tabindex="-1" (e.g. MediaCommentsSection.tsx:40), so after "jumping" a keyboard user's focus is still on the link at the top — the next Tab continues from the nav and they must traverse every control between anyway. The jump feature is effectively visual-only for keyboard users.
fix: After scrolling, move focus to the destination: give each section container tabindex={-1} and call el.focus({ preventScroll: true }) alongside smoothScrollIntoView (wrap in the existing scroll helper so all jump links inherit it).

verdict.reasoning: BirdingStats.tsx:449 (and LifeList.tsx:505) call e.preventDefault() + smoothScrollIntoView, and lib/scroll.ts only scrolls — it never moves focus; the targets are plain divs (SectionCard in statsPrimitives.tsx, MediaCommentsSection.tsx:40) with no tabindex. preventDefault suppresses the browser's native fragment-navigation focus relocation, so after a jump the next Tab resumes from the nav chip — the feature is visual-only for keyboard users. The suggested fix (tabindex=-1 on targets + focus({preventScroll:true}) folded into the shared scroll helper) is correct and convention-conforming.
verdict.fixNote: Put tabIndex={-1} on the SectionCard root div (statsPrimitives.tsx) so all nine Statistics targets inherit it, add the same to the #media-comments div in MediaCommentsSection.tsx, and add a jumpTo(el) wrapper in lib/scroll.ts that calls smoothScrollIntoView(el) then el.focus({ preventScroll: true }); switch the three preventDefault call sites (BirdingStats.tsx:449, LifeList.tsx:505) to it. Add :focus-visible-only outline styling (or outline: none on [tabindex="-1"]) so the programmatic focus doesn't paint the green focus ring on the whole card for mouse users.

title: Help overlay closes without restoring focus to the control that opened it
description: HelpDocs correctly focuses its Close button on open and traps Tab (re-querying per keydown — the best trap in the codebase), but on close (Escape at line 257 or the Close button) the overlay unmounts with focus inside it and nothing restores focus: App.tsx:1205 is just `onClose={() => setHelpOpen(false)}`. Focus drops to <body>, so a keyboard user who opened Help from the footer Help button, Settings' 'Open help', or the Welcome screen must Tab from the top of the document to get back to where they were. Standard dialog behavior is to return focus to the invoking element.
fix: Capture `document.activeElement` when helpOpen becomes true (or pass an opener ref) and `.focus()` it after the overlay unmounts; same for the Welcome-screen-opened case.

verdict.reasoning: Verified App.tsx:1205 is bare `onClose={() => setHelpOpen(false)}`, HelpDocs has no unmount cleanup, and no activeElement capture/restore exists anywhere in src/ — focus is inside the unmounting overlay (Close button focused on mount) and drops to <body> on both Escape (line 257) and the Close button. All three openers (footer App.tsx:1113, Settings.tsx:1078, WelcomeScreen.tsx:100) are affected. ACCESSIBILITY.md's Focus Management section only covers the map filter panel (which does restore focus), so not disclosed; moderate is the right severity.
verdict.fixNote: The capture-activeElement-in-HelpDocs approach works because the lazy mount uses `fallback={null}` (focus is still on the opener at first effect time), but the capture effect must be declared BEFORE the existing `closeRef.current?.focus()` effect at line 251, with the restore in that effect's cleanup: `useEffect(() => { const opener = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null; return () => opener?.focus() }, [])`. This covers Escape, the Close button, and all three openers with no prop plumbing.

title: Closing the Help overlay drops focus to <body> instead of returning to the Help button
description: HelpDocs correctly focuses its Close button on open and traps Tab, but onClose (Close button or Escape) simply unmounts the overlay (App.tsx:1203-1205 just sets helpOpen false) — focus falls to document.body and the keyboard user restarts from the top of the page. The Map Explorer filter sidebar (filtersButtonRef refocus) and the TabNav dropdown (close(true)) both restore focus correctly; HelpDocs is the inconsistent one. It can be opened from three places (footer, Welcome screen, Settings), so the opener should be remembered.
fix: Capture document.activeElement when the overlay mounts and restore focus to it in a cleanup effect (covers all three openers without prop plumbing).

verdict.reasoning: This is the same defect as index 27 (exact duplicate, different cited line): App.tsx:1203-1205 just sets helpOpen false, no capture/restore code exists, and focus verifiably falls to <body>; the contrast with the map filter sidebar's correct refocus is accurate. Confirmed, but minor understates it — a keyboard user re-Tabs from the document top after every Help close, and the identical finding at index 27 is rated moderate, so aligned to moderate. Should be merged with index 27 as one finding.
verdict.fixNote: Same fix as index 27: a mount-time effect in HelpDocs declared before the closeRef-focus effect, capturing document.activeElement and refocusing it in the cleanup — covers all three openers without prop plumbing.

title: Map Explorer async error messages are silent to assistive tech
description: The hotspot search error (:1006-1011) and media-targets search error (:1227-1232) render as plain styled divs after an async failure — no role="alert" or aria-live, so a screen-reader user who pressed "Find Hotspots"/"Find Recent Sightings" gets no feedback that the request failed (the role="status" loading chip just disappears). Other error paths in the app do this correctly (ChecklistComparer.tsx:372, App.tsx:720, DropZone.tsx:132).
fix: Add role="alert" to both error divs (matching ChecklistComparer's pattern).

verdict.reasoning: Verified: hotspotsError (1006-1011) and targetsError (1227-1232) render as plain divs with an aria-less AlertCircle icon, no role/aria-live anywhere in MapExplorer per grep, and the role=status loading chip (1437) simply unmounts on failure — so an SR user gets no failure feedback. Cited reference implementations (ChecklistComparer 372, App 720, DropZone 132) all exist, and role=alert on these two divs is the correct house-pattern fix. Note this is a strict subset of finding 11 (same two MapExplorer locations); confirmed independently at moderate, but the two should be deduplicated when applying fixes.

title: Light theme: accent-colored text marginally fails on tinted/page backgrounds (4.03–4.32:1)
description: Light --sr-accent #2D8653 passes on white surfaces (4.52:1) but fails where it is used on anything tinted: on --sr-accent-bg = 4.03:1 — the app-wide active-state pattern (ghost buttons, active filter pills, the tab dropdown's selected option TabNav.tsx:309-314, SpeciesPanel count badge :44-45; background:'var(--sr-accent-bg)' + accent text appears in 14 files); on --sr-bg = 4.32:1 — the active tab label (tab bar sits directly on the page background, App.tsx:583) and the footer 'Up to date' status (App.tsx:1154); on --sr-surface-subtle = 4.11:1. Dark theme passes everywhere (7.75–10.35:1).
fix: In light theme use --sr-accent-strong (#1A5C38; 7.12:1 on accent-bg, ~6.7:1 on bg) for accent-as-TEXT on tinted/page backgrounds, keeping --sr-accent for fills, borders and focus rings; or darken light --sr-accent to ~#27764A so it clears 4.5:1 on --sr-accent-bg.

verdict.reasoning: Independent WCAG relative-luminance math reproduces every reported ratio exactly: light #2D8653 is 4.03:1 on --sr-accent-bg #E8F5EE, 4.32:1 on --sr-bg #F9FAFB, 4.11:1 on --sr-surface-subtle #F4F4F5 (4.52:1 on white passes; dark theme passes at 7.75-10.35). The pairs genuinely co-occur — dropdown selected option (TabNav 309-314), SpeciesPanel count badge (11px accent text on accent-bg), active tab label over the body's --sr-bg background, footer 'Up to date' span — all normal-size text requiring 4.5:1, and 24 files reference --sr-accent-bg. ACCESSIBILITY.md claims AA for primary interface colors with only chart-bar labels excepted, so this is a real undisclosed AA failure; the suggested --sr-accent-strong fix is convention-compliant (token defined in both themes; verified 7.12:1 on accent-bg, 7.64:1 on bg) and the alternative #27764A verifies at 4.96/5.32/5.56.

title: Primary navigation and header have no landmark exposure; HelpDocs TOC nav is unlabeled
description: Three related landmark-structure gaps (merged): (1) Desktop tab bar: <nav aria-label="Main navigation" role="tablist"> (TabNav.tsx:105-108) — the explicit role="tablist" overrides <nav>'s implicit navigation role, so no navigation landmark exists anywhere on the page; screen-reader landmark navigation (rotor/landmark list) shows no way to find the primary navigation. (2) Collapsed mode: TabDropdown renders in a plain <div> (TabNav.tsx:228) with no nav landmark at all, so narrow/mobile users also get no navigation landmark. (3) The app header with branding and tagline is a plain styled div (App.tsx:570), not <header>/banner, leaving it outside any landmark. By contrast <main> (App.tsx:586) and the footer role="contentinfo" (App.tsx:1100) are correct. Additionally the HelpDocs TOC <nav> (HelpDocs.tsx:347) has no accessible name, so it announces as an anonymous navigation region inside the documentation dialog.
evidence: TabNav.tsx:105-108 `<nav aria-label="Main navigation" ... role="tablist">`; TabNav.tsx:228 dropdown wrapper is `<div style={{ padding: '12px 16px', position: 'relative' }} ref={wrapRef}>`; App.tsx:570 `<div className="sr-header" ...>`; HelpDocs.tsx:347 `<nav style={{...}}>` with no aria-label.
suggestedFix:
Wrap the tablist in a labeled nav instead of putting role="tablist" on the nav itself:
…
; wrap TabDropdown's container in the same
; change the App header div to
(banner); add aria-label="Documentation contents" to the HelpDocs TOC nav.

verdict.reasoning: All four citations verified: role="tablist" on the <nav> (TabNav.tsx:105-108) overrides its implicit navigation role, so desktop mode exposes no navigation landmark; collapsed mode's wrapper (TabNav.tsx:228) is a bare div with none either; the branding header (App.tsx:570) is a plain div outside any landmark; HelpDocs.tsx:347 is an unlabeled <nav>. Screen-reader landmark navigation therefore cannot locate the primary navigation in either mode — a genuine 1.3.1-adjacent structural gap, distinct from confirmed #33 (which is about dangling tabpanel aria-labelledby, not landmark exposure). Moderate is fair given main and contentinfo exist but the primary nav is unfindable by landmark.
verdict.fixNote: Fix is correct (nav wrapping a div[role=tablist] is the canonical pattern). Use the same accessible name (e.g. aria-label="Main navigation") on both the desktop and collapsed-mode <nav> wrappers so the landmark announces identically across modes; keep the sr-header className when converting the header div to <header>.

title: Tab key in the collapsed nav dropdown unmounts the focused option before the browser moves focus
description: In TabDropdown, the menu's Tab case calls `close(false)` without preventDefault, intending the browser to move focus onward naturally. But focus lives on a menu option (real DOM focus, line 176/182), and React 18 flushes the discrete keydown update synchronously — the listbox (rendered behind `{open && ...}`, line 265) unmounts and the focused option is removed BEFORE the browser performs the default Tab traversal. Focus falls to <body>, so the default Tab then lands on the first focusable element in the document instead of the control after the trigger. On narrow/mobile widths this dropdown is the app's primary navigation, so Tab-to-leave silently teleports keyboard users to the top of the page. (Escape, by contrast, correctly returns focus to the trigger via close(true).)
fix: On Tab: `e.preventDefault(); close(true)` then let the user Tab from the trigger — or preventDefault and programmatically focus the element after the trigger. Either keeps focus deterministic.

verdict.reasoning: Lines 209-211 call close(false) with no preventDefault while real DOM focus sits on an option inside the conditionally-rendered listbox (line 265); under React 19's synchronous discrete-event flush the focused option unmounts before the browser's default Tab traversal, dropping focus to body. On narrow widths this dropdown is the primary navigation, so the 2.4.3 impact and moderate severity are fair. Escape's close(true) contrast claim also checks out (lines 205-207).
verdict.fixNote: Simplest fix: in the Tab case call close(true) WITHOUT preventDefault. Inside close(), triggerRef.current?.focus() runs synchronously before React flushes the setOpen(false) unmount, so focus is on the trigger when the browser performs the default Tab — focus then moves naturally to the element after the trigger in ONE keystroke (and Shift+Tab to the element before it), with no extra keypress the suggested preventDefault+close(true) variant would require.

title: Collapsed dropdown nav orphans every tabpanel (dangling aria-labelledby, no tablist)
description: All panels in App.tsx use aria-labelledby="tab-{id}" (e.g. App.tsx:590). In the collapsed TabDropdown mode the id="tab-{id}" elements exist only on the listbox options while the menu is open (TabNav.tsx:298) — with the menu closed (the normal state) the visible role="tabpanel" references a nonexistent id and there is no tablist/tab anywhere in the tree, so the tab/tabpanel relationship ACCESSIBILITY.md claims ("Tabs and their panels are linked with the correct tab/tabpanel roles") is broken precisely for the zoom/narrow-viewport users who get the dropdown. The dropdown also replaces tab semantics with listbox semantics, leaving orphaned tabpanels.
fix: Give panels a stable label that doesn't depend on the bar variant — e.g. aria-label={TAB_LABELS[id]} on each panel (or keep aria-labelledby but render persistent visually-hidden label elements), and use distinct ids for dropdown options.

verdict.reasoning: All ten App.tsx panels (lines 588-1073) use role=tabpanel + aria-labelledby="tab-{id}", but in collapsed mode the only tab-{id} elements are dropdown options (TabNav.tsx:298) that exist only while the menu is open and carry role=option, not role=tab — so in the normal closed state every labelledby idref dangles and the tabpanels are orphaned with no tablist in the tree. ACCESSIBILITY.md line 19 explicitly claims 'Tabs and their panels are linked with the correct tab/tabpanel roles' and its only disclosed contrast/structure exception is chart-bar labels, so this contradicts a published statement rather than being disclosed. Moderate is fair: it breaks panel names and structure for the entire narrow-viewport/zoom audience.

title: WelcomeScreen modal has no focus trap; map fullscreen overlay leaves hidden chrome tabbable
description: WelcomeScreen declares role="dialog" aria-modal="true" and handles only Escape (line 21) — there is no Tab containment and the app behind it is not inert, so tabbing past "Explore the app first" moves focus into the fully obscured app underneath (the overlay background is opaque var(--sr-bg)); a sighted keyboard user loses the focus indicator entirely while aria-modal simultaneously tells screen readers the background doesn't exist. The map fullscreen mode has the same background-tabbing issue: it is a CSS overlay (panel fixed inset 0, App.tsx:1031-1042) and only body scroll is locked (App.tsx:390-395), so the tab bar and footer remain in the tab order while visually covered. (Not a 2.1.2 trap — focus can always leave — but focus lands on invisible controls.)
fix: Give WelcomeScreen the same Tab-wrap handler HelpDocs uses (HelpDocs.tsx:256-274). For map fullscreen, set inert (or aria-hidden + tabindex management) on the sibling app chrome while active, and consider Escape-to-exit-fullscreen as polish.

verdict.reasoning: WelcomeScreen.tsx:19-24 handles only Escape with no Tab containment while declaring aria-modal="true", and App.tsx:1195-1201 mounts it inside the full app tree, so the obscured tab bar/footer remain tabbable behind the opaque var(--sr-bg) overlay. The map fullscreen claim also holds: App.tsx:1031-1033 is a fixed inset-0 z-1200 CSS overlay and App.tsx:389-395 locks only body scroll — no inert/aria-hidden/focus-trap exists anywhere in frontend/src. ACCESSIBILITY.md's Focus Management section discloses only the Map Explorer filter-panel trap, not this gap; moderate is the right severity (focus lands on invisible controls but is recoverable, not a 2.1.2 trap).
verdict.fixNote: The suggested fix is correct and convention-consistent — HelpDocs.tsx:258-274 has exactly the referenced Tab-wrap handler. Two refinements: WelcomeScreen should query focusables from a ref on its own root div (it has no DOM id, unlike HelpDocs' getElementById('sr-help-overlay')), and for map fullscreen the `inert` attribute is safe in both desktop targets (WKWebView/Safari 15.5+, WebView2) — apply it to the sibling tabpanels, TabNav, and footer while mapFullscreen && activeTab === 'map-explorer', clearing it in the same effect cleanup as the existing body scroll lock at App.tsx:390-395. Update ACCESSIBILITY.md's Focus Management section in the same change per CLAUDE.md.

title: Document title is static; active view is never reflected in the page/window title
description: The title is "SnowRaven" (index.html:7) and nothing in src/ ever writes document.title (grep finds no occurrences); the Tauri window title is likewise static (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:14). Because the app is a true single page with an in-page tab widget and no routing (no pushState/hash/router anywhere), the static title technically satisfies 2.4.2. But with ten distinct views (Weather, Species Detail, Map Explorer, Statistics, Settings, …), updating the title on tab change would aid orientation for screen-reader users, browser-tab/window switchers, and history — standard SPA practice.
suggestedFix: On tab change in App.tsx, set document.title = `${activeLabel} — SnowRaven` (a small useEffect keyed on activeTab); this also updates the desktop window title in Tauri.

verdict.reasoning: Verified: index.html:7 title is static, no document.title writes anywhere in frontend/src, no routing, and tauri.conf.json:14 hardcodes the window title. Not a 2.4.2 conformance failure (single page, no navigations) but a fairly-flagged SPA best-practice item with real if small orientation benefit for screen-reader users and tab/window switchers across ten distinct views. Severity minor is correct; not disclosed in ACCESSIBILITY.md.
verdict.fixNote: The useEffect-on-activeTab setting document.title is right for web, but the claim that it 'also updates the desktop window title in Tauri' is wrong — Tauri v2 does not sync document.title to the native window title. Behind isTauri() also call getCurrentWindow().setTitle(...) from @tauri-apps/api/window, and add core:window:allow-set-title to src-tauri/capabilities/default.json (core:default does not include set-title).

title: role="status" loading indicators mount already containing their text (announcement unreliable)
description: Loading/status chips are conditionally rendered elements that carry role="status" AND their message in the same insertion: TabLoading (App.tsx:125), tide states (App.tsx:837-845), MapExplorer loading chip (:1437), BirdingStats (:464, :883), AtlasLayer (:230), WeatherTidePanel (:165-235). Live regions must exist before their content changes; regions inserted with initial text are announced by some AT/browser combos and skipped by others, so loading/unavailable states are inconsistently conveyed. Pattern issue — reported once for all locations.
fix: Keep a persistent (always-mounted, possibly empty) role="status" container per area and swap its text content, rather than mounting the live region together with its message.

verdict.reasoning: All cited instances verified: TabLoading (App.tsx:125, also the Suspense fallbacks), tide chips (:837-845), MapExplorer:1437, BirdingStats:464/:883, AtlasLayer:230, WeatherTidePanel:165-235 — every one is a conditionally-mounted element carrying role="status" together with its message, which AT announces inconsistently since the live region doesn't pre-exist its content change. Real but low-impact (loading-state awareness only; the loaded content itself is perceivable), so minor is the right severity and it's fairly batched as one pattern finding. The persistent-container fix is the standard remedy; note that for the Suspense fallbacks (TabLoading) the persistent region must live outside the Suspense boundary.

title: No skip link to bypass the header/tab bar before main content
description: There is no skip-to-main-content link anywhere in the app (grep for skip-link patterns across src/, index.css, App.css, globals.css, and main.tsx returns nothing). The branding header (App.tsx:570) and TabNav (App.tsx:583) render before <main> (App.tsx:586). Impact is low — strictly, 2.4.1 is satisfiable via the existing <main> landmark (technique ARIA11), the header contains no focusable elements, and both TabNav variants are a single tab stop (desktop roving tabindex at TabNav.tsx:132; collapsed dropdown is one trigger button) — so a sighted keyboard user pays only one extra Tab per page load. Reported as a best-practice gap rather than a conformance failure.
evidence: App.tsx:570 header div and :583 <TabNav> precede <main> at :586; no element or CSS class implementing a skip link exists in the codebase.
suggestedFix:
Add a visually-hidden-until-focused anchor as the first child of the root div: Skip to main content, give
id="sr-main" and tabIndex={-1}, and style .sr-skip-link to appear on :focus (positioned fixed, z-index above 1200 since overlays use 1200).

verdict.reasoning: Verified: no skip link exists anywhere in src/ or index.html; header (App.tsx:570) has no focusable elements, both TabNav modes are one tab stop, and <main> (App.tsx:586) provides a landmark, so 2.4.1 is technically satisfied (ARIA11) and the cost is one extra Tab. The auditor honestly framed it as a best-practice gap and rated it minor, which is correct — landmarks help AT users but not sighted keyboard users, so a skip link is the standard remaining piece. Fairly-flagged polish item, not pedantry.
verdict.fixNote: Suggested fix is sound; style .sr-skip-link with var(--sr-*) tokens added to both :root and [data-theme="dark"] in globals.css (per the theming convention), and z-index above 1200 as noted since the map fullscreen overlay and dropdown both sit at 1200.

title: Bare "↗" glyph checklist links rely on title attribute alone; footer "SnowRaven" link hides its GitHub destination
description: Two weak link-purpose patterns (merged): (1) BirdingStats Highlights/Records links render the single glyph "↗" as their only content with title="Open checklist" (BirdingStats.tsx:1332, 1564, 1589). The accessible name comes only from the title fallback — fragile across AT, invisible to sighted keyboard users (title tooltips don't appear on focus), unavailable on touch — and the repeated identical name "Open checklist" is distinguished only by surrounding card/row context. (2) The footer link whose text is "SnowRaven" (App.tsx:1101-1110) actually navigates to the GitHub repository; neither the link text nor its programmatic context ("SnowRaven · Self-hosted Birding Tools") reveals that destination.
evidence: BirdingStats.tsx:1332 `↗`; App.tsx:1101-1109 `SnowRaven`.
suggestedFix: Give the ↗ links a real accessible name including their distinguishing context, e.g. aria-label={`Open ${card.label} checklist on eBird`} (keep title for sighted hover if desired); change the footer link text or aria-label to "SnowRaven on GitHub".

verdict.reasoning: This is a merged finding: part (1) — the bare ↗ checklist links in BirdingStats (verified at 1332, 1564, 1589, title="Open checklist" only) — is a duplicate of confirmed finding #53 (same elements, same root cause: inadequate accessible naming of the repeated ↗ links). Part (2) is real and distinct: App.tsx:1101-1110 footer link with text 'SnowRaven' navigates to the GitHub repo with nothing in the text or contentinfo context revealing the destination, while App.tsx:898 already demonstrates the correct pattern for the SnowRaven Mini link. Confirmed on the footer-link aspect only; minor severity fits a single ambiguous 2.4.4 link.
verdict.fixNote: Treat the ↗-naming portion as covered by confirmed #53 and fix only the footer here: give the footer anchor aria-label="SnowRaven on GitHub (opens in new tab)" (or change the visible text), matching the existing SnowRaven Mini pattern at App.tsx:898.

title: The 'loading-saved' phase on four data tabs is a bare unlabeled spinner — nothing is announced and nothing names the state
wcag: 4.1.3 Status Messages AA (also 1.1.1 Non-text Content A)
description: While a tab parses the stored CSV (the phase every visit passes through before the data or the SetupRequired panel appears), four tabs replace their entire panel with a centered Loader2 SVG and nothing else: Checklists.tsx:468-470 (the icon is even explicitly aria-hidden, leaving zero accessible content in the panel), LifeList.tsx:362-364, SpeciesDetail.tsx:408-410, and BreedingCodeList.tsx:174-176. There is no role="status", no aria-label, and no visible text, so a screen-reader user lands in an empty tabpanel with no indication anything is happening. Every other loading state in the app does this correctly and was recorded as a pass (boot skeleton role=status 'Loading SnowRaven', App.tsx TabLoading role=status with text, BirdingStats.tsx:464 computing status, SnowMap style placeholder) — these four bare spinners are the stragglers. Distinct from prior finding i=74 (which covers role=status nodes that mount with text already present — these have no status semantics at all).
evidence: Checklists.tsx:469 `<Loader2 size={24} strokeWidth={2} className="spin" style={{ color: 'var(--sr-accent)' }} aria-hidden />` as the sole child of the phase's wrapper div; identical Loader2-only blocks at LifeList.tsx:363, SpeciesDetail.tsx:409, BreedingCodeList.tsx:~176 (those three without even aria-hidden, but with no text either).
suggestedFix: Give each wrapper div role="status" and an aria-label (e.g. 'Loading saved eBird data') — or add visible text next to the spinner as WeatherTidePanel does ('Loading weather…') — and keep the SVG aria-hidden, matching the App.tsx TabLoading pattern.

verdict.reasoning: All four cited blocks verified: Checklists.tsx:466-472 (Loader2 with aria-hidden as the panel's sole content), LifeList.tsx:360-366, SpeciesDetail.tsx:406-412, BreedingCodeList.tsx:172-178 — no role='status', no aria-label, no text, leaving an empty tabpanel during the loading-saved phase every visit passes through. Genuinely distinct from confirmed i=74, which covers nodes that already have role='status' but mount with text present; these have no status semantics at all. Not disclosed in ACCESSIBILITY.md and not present in either findings file.
verdict.fixNote: Matching the App.tsx TabLoading pattern (role='status' + label on the wrapper, SVG aria-hidden) is right; note per confirmed finding i=74 that a status node mounting with its label may still not be announced by all SRs, but it at least names the state for users who land in the panel — fixing both together would mean mounting the empty status container first and inserting the label.

title: External links open new windows without any indication (inconsistent across the app)
description: 43 target="_blank" anchors exist across ~20 component files; only two indicate the behavior — App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 use "(opens in new tab)" in aria-label. All others give no warning, including every link in the Help documentation (HelpDocs.tsx:61 renders all HELP.md links with target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" and no indication), the footer GitHub link (App.tsx:1101-1110), SpeciesLinks.tsx:20/45 (whose aria-labels "View X on eBird" omit it), LifeListTable.tsx media-count links, BirdingStats.tsx checklist/region links (15 instances), Checklists.tsx, MapExplorer.tsx, SpeciesDetail.tsx, NamedBirdRow.tsx, Settings.tsx, WeatherTidePanel.tsx, MediaCommentsSection.tsx, MediaStatsSections.tsx, ChecklistComparer.tsx, SightingsMap.tsx, map/HotspotMarkers.tsx, map/TargetMarkers.tsx, AtlasLayer.tsx, speciesDetail/ui.tsx, CommentText.tsx. Unexpected context changes disorient screen-reader and cognitive-disability users; the app already has the right pattern in two places — it just isn't applied consistently.
evidence: HelpDocs.tsx:61 `<a key={ki++} href={lm[2]} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer"` with no new-window indication; grep shows 43 target="_blank" instances, only App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 carry "(opens in new tab)".
suggestedFix: Adopt one shared ExternalA component (or extend SpeciesLinks' pattern) that appends "(opens in new tab)" to the accessible name (visually-hidden span or aria-label suffix) and use it for all target="_blank" anchors, including HelpDocs' renderInline link branch.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by grep: exactly 43 target="_blank" anchors across 20 component files, with only App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 announcing '(opens in new tab)'; HelpDocs.tsx renders every documentation link target="_blank" with no indication and SpeciesLinks.tsx aria-labels omit it. This is the new-window-indication aspect, explicitly distinct from confirmed #53 (which covers the ↗ links' accessible names), so not a duplicate. Correctly scoped as advisory (G201; 3.2.5 is AAA), so minor severity is right; not disclosed in ACCESSIBILITY.md.
verdict.fixNote: A shared external-link component is sound; prefer a visually-hidden span suffix over aria-label so existing link text is preserved, and where an aria-label already exists (SpeciesLinks, icon-only links) append to the label, matching the wording already used at App.tsx:748/898. For icon-only favicon links keep title in sync with the label.

title: WCAG 2.2 forward-looking: several form controls are under the 24px minimum target size
description: Forward-looking 2.2 delta only. The atlas overlay role="switch" buttons are 38x22px (MapExplorer.tsx:726, :759, :788 — 22px tall, under the 24px minimum), and several zero-padding text buttons are ~16-18px tall: the API-key Show/Hide button (Settings.tsx:363-373, padding 0, 0.75rem text), the 'Clear filter' underline buttons (LifeList.tsx:694-703, Checklists.tsx:685-690, SpeciesDetail.tsx:658-667), and the 'Go to Settings →' banner buttons (App.tsx:611-619, padding 0). Most currently escape 2.5.8 via the spacing exception (no adjacent target within 24px), but that is fragile under layout changes and the small targets are already hard for motor-impaired users under 2.1 best practice.
fix: Bump the switch buttons to at least 24px tall (e.g. 44x24 track) and give the zero-padding text buttons enough padding (or min-height: 24px with negative-margin compensation) to reach a 24x24 hit area.

verdict.reasoning: All cited controls verified: the three hand-rolled role=switch buttons are 38x22 (MapExplorer.tsx:726, :759, :788 — 22px tall, under 24), and the padding-0 text buttons exist as described in Settings.tsx:363-373 (Show/Hide), LifeList.tsx:694-703 / Checklists.tsx:685-690 / SpeciesDetail.tsx:658-667 (Clear filter), and App.tsx:611-619 (Go to Settings), all at 0.75rem with no padding (~17px hit height). The finding honestly frames itself as a forward-looking WCAG 2.2 delta and acknowledges the spacing exception currently covers most of them, so minor is the right severity.
verdict.fixNote: The codebase already has a shared ui/ToggleSwitch.tsx (a 30px-tall role=switch button with the label inside) — prefer migrating the three inline atlas switches to it, or if the label-left/switch-right layout must stay, bump the bare track to >=24px tall (e.g. 44x24). For the zero-padding text buttons, padding (or min-height 24 with negative-margin compensation) as originally suggested is fine.

title: Map Explorer Filters accordion button lacks aria-expanded
description: The collapsible filter panel toggle in the sightings sidebar (button at :836, panel collapsed via max-height 0) exposes no expanded/collapsed state — the only cue is the rotated chevron. Every other disclosure in the app does carry aria-expanded (NamedBirdRow.tsx:36, ChecklistComparer.tsx:76/:440, TabNav.tsx:234).
fix: Add aria-expanded={filterOpen} (and optionally aria-controls) to the Filters button.

verdict.reasoning: The Filters disclosure button (MapExplorer.tsx:835-847) carries no aria-expanded; the only state cue is the rotated ChevronDown, and the panel collapses via maxHeight 0. Verified the cited convention claim: NamedBirdRow.tsx:36, ChecklistComparer.tsx:76 and :440, and TabNav.tsx:234 all set aria-expanded on their disclosures, so this is an isolated omission. Minor is right and the suggested one-attribute fix (aria-expanded={filterOpen}, optionally aria-controls) is correct and conventional.

title: Tablist lacks Home/End keys (APG completeness)
wcag: 2.1.1 Keyboard A (advisory — APG tabs pattern; no AA failure)
description: The desktop tab bar implements roving tabindex with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight + wrap (TabNav.tsx:109-123) but not Home/End to jump to the first/last tab, which the WAI-ARIA APG tabs pattern recommends (the collapsed dropdown DOES implement Home/End at lines 197-204, so the two modes are inconsistent). With 10+ tabs this is several extra keystrokes, not a barrier — forward-looking polish only.
fix: Add Home → items[0] and End → items[items.length-1] cases to the tablist onKeyDown, mirroring the dropdown's handling.

verdict.reasoning: TabBar's tablist onKeyDown (TabNav.tsx:109-123) handles only ArrowLeft/ArrowRight while the collapsed dropdown implements Home/End (lines 197-204), confirming both the gap and the cross-mode inconsistency. The finding correctly self-classifies as advisory APG polish with no AA failure (Home/End are optional in the APG tabs pattern, and arrow wrapping caps traversal at ~half the tab count), so minor is the right severity. The suggested fix mirrors an existing in-file pattern and is sound.

title: TabDropdown listbox misuses aria-activedescendant and trigger lacks aria-controls
description: The dropdown menu manages focus by moving DOM focus to the option buttons (roving), yet the listbox container also sets aria-activedescendant — on an element that itself never receives focus (no tabindex), where the attribute has no effect, and pointing at the SELECTED tab rather than the focused option. All options are also tabIndex={0} (the pattern expects -1 with the container or roving single stop), and the trigger (:233) has aria-haspopup/aria-expanded but no aria-controls referencing the listbox. Functionally usable (DOM focus carries the announcements) but the ARIA contradicts the actual focus model.
fix: Remove aria-activedescendant (DOM focus already tracks the active option), set option tabIndex={-1}, give the listbox an id, and add aria-controls to the trigger.

verdict.reasoning: All claims verify in current code: line 269 sets aria-activedescendant={`tab-${activeTab}`} on a listbox div that never receives focus (no tabindex) and points at the selected rather than focused option, options are tabIndex={0} (line 300) despite roving DOM focus, and the trigger (lines 229-237) lacks aria-controls (the listbox also has no id to reference). The component is functionally usable since DOM focus carries announcements, so minor is the correct severity for this ARIA-contradicts-focus-model issue. The suggested fix (drop activedescendant, tabIndex={-1} on options, listbox id + trigger aria-controls) is correct — programmatic .focus() works on tabindex=-1 elements, so the existing focusItem logic is unaffected.

title: Southern-hemisphere moon emoji mirroring makes screen readers announce the wrong phase
description: The moon-phase emoji is the ONLY carrier of moon-phase information in night weather blocks (no adjacent text line — the condition emoji, by contrast, is followed by the textual condition on the next line). For northern latitudes this is acceptable: SRs read Unicode emoji names ("waxing gibbous moon"), which match the phase. But MOON_SOUTH deliberately swaps to the visually-mirrored emoji for lat < 0, so a southern-hemisphere waxing crescent is rendered as 🌘 whose Unicode name is "waning crescent moon" — a SR (and anyone hovering for the character name) hears the opposite phase. Constrained by the paste-into-eBird output format, so an in-app-only fix is appropriate.
fix: Where the formatted block is displayed in-app (the <pre> on the Weather tab and WeatherTidePanel), wrap the header emoji run in a span with an aria-label giving the true phase name (e.g. "cloudy, waxing crescent moon"), or append the phase as text in the in-app rendering only.

verdict.reasoning: weatherFormatter.ts:93-102 swaps to mirrored emoji for lat<0, so all six asymmetric phases carry the opposite phase's Unicode name (verified: southern waxing crescent emits 🌘 'waning crescent moon'); the emoji is the block's only phase carrier (formatWeatherBody emits `${emoji}${moon}` with no phase text line) and renders as raw text in the Weather tab <pre> (App.tsx:827) and WeatherTidePanel's MonoBlock, where SRs announce it by character name. ACCESSIBILITY.md does not disclose this — it actually claims icon-only info carries hidden text labels. Minor is fair: narrow trigger (southern hemisphere + night checklist + SR) but the announced info is actively wrong, a genuine 1.1.1 failure.
verdict.fixNote: In the in-app renderings only (App.tsx Weather-tab <pre> ~line 811 and WeatherTidePanel's MonoBlock), split off the header line and wrap the emoji run in <span role="img" aria-label="..."> — a bare span aria-label is not reliably honored by SRs without role="img". Derive the true phase name by exporting it from weatherFormatter.ts (e.g. a moonPhaseName(unixTs) beside moonPhaseEmoji, or reverse-lookup the rendered emoji's index in MOON_SOUTH when lat < 0; northern emoji names are already correct). Do NOT change formatWeatherBody's output string — it is byte-locked with backend/formatters/weather.py and the commentBlocks.ts stripper anchors on the unspaced contiguous emoji run.

title: Desktop: no page-zoom path exists — Ctrl/Cmd+= is a no-op and the window floor is 800 CSS px, so the 1.4.10 reflow condition is unreachable and ACCESSIBILITY.md's zoom sentence is false on desktop
wcag: 1.4.10 Reflow AA (WCAG2ICT) / 1.4.4 Resize Text AA — plus published-claim accuracy
description: The main window sets minWidth: 800 (tauri.conf.json:17) and does NOT set zoomHotkeysEnabled, which defaults to false (verified in the repo's own @tauri-apps/cli config.schema.json: WindowConfig.zoomHotkeysEnabled, "default": false — on Windows it controls WebView2's IsZoomControlEnabled, i.e. Ctrl+hotkey AND Ctrl+wheel zoom; on macOS/Linux it injects a JS polyfill). No Rust code wires any menu, accelerator, or zoom command (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:48-68 registers only plugins and 5 commands; main.rs is 6 lines), and capabilities/default.json lacks the webview:allow-set-webview-zoom permission the macOS/Linux polyfill would require even if enabled. Net effect, derived statically: in the desktop app, Ctrl/Cmd +/−/wheel zoom does nothing on any platform, and the window can never present narrower than 800 CSS px. Consequences under WCAG2ICT reasoning: (1) the web audit's 1.4.10 verification at 320 CSS px and its 1.4.4 verification via browser zoom are both unreachable on desktop — the only enlargement mechanism is the in-app Text Size control capped at 200% (lib/textScale.ts:11, TEXT_SCALES max 2). That satisfies SC 1.4.4's 200% requirement, but the 400%-equivalent enlarged view SC 1.4.10 presupposes (1280px viewport at 400% = 320 CSS px) can never be produced, so the desktop product conforms to 1.4.10 only vacuously, and a desktop low-vision user who needs more than 2x enlargement has no in-app path at all (a web user has browser zoom to 400%+, stackable with Text Size). OS display scaling enlarges physical pixels but cannot push the window below 800 CSS px either. (2) ACCESSIBILITY.md:39 states "Browser/page zoom (Ctrl/Cmd +/−) works too" within a statement that explicitly covers the desktop app (line 3: "It runs in the browser and as a desktop app") — that sentence is false on desktop, and it sits two lines below line 37's own correct disclosure that the desktop app "has no browser zoom of its own", an internal contradiction. Status: the config default is documented and there is zero zoom wiring anywhere in src-tauri, so this is asserted statically; a live desktop run to confirm the hotkeys are inert is advisable (needs-runtime-verification as a formality only).
evidence: tauri.conf.json:12-19 window config contains only title/width/height/minWidth/minHeight; node_modules/@tauri-apps/cli/config.schema.json WindowConfig.zoomHotkeysEnabled → "default": false, macOS/Linux polyfill "Requires `webview:allow-set-webview-zoom` permission"; src-tauri/capabilities/default.json has no webview:* permission; ACCESSIBILITY.md:39 "Browser/page zoom (Ctrl/Cmd +/−) works too." vs :37 "the desktop app, which has no browser zoom of its own".
suggestedFix: Set "zoomHotkeysEnabled": true on the main window in tauri.conf.json and add "webview:allow-set-webview-zoom" to capabilities/default.json — Tauri then provides Ctrl/Cmd +/− page zoom from 20% to 1000% on all three desktop platforms, giving the desktop product a real 1.4.10/1.4.4 path (verify on a live build, especially the macOS/Linux polyfill). Independently and immediately, reword ACCESSIBILITY.md line 39 to scope the page-zoom sentence to the browser build (e.g. "In the browser, page zoom (Ctrl/Cmd +/−) works too") so the published statement is true for desktop, and update it again when the hotkeys ship.

verdict.reasoning: Every static claim verified: tauri.conf.json:17 sets minWidth 800 with no zoomHotkeysEnabled (schema default false, macOS/Linux polyfill needs webview:allow-set-webview-zoom which capabilities/default.json lacks), src-tauri/src/lib.rs wires no zoom, and TEXT_SCALES caps at 2 — so the desktop app genuinely offers no enlargement beyond 200% and no path to a 320-CSS-px-equivalent view. But no WCAG 2.1 AA SC is actually failed: 1.4.4 is satisfied by the 200% Text Size control and 1.4.10 is vacuously met (the condition is unreachable, not violated), and ACCESSIBILITY.md:37 itself already discloses the desktop app 'has no browser zoom of its own', leaving only line 39's ambiguous sentence as the doc defect. Real and worth fixing (cheap config change, genuine benefit to low-vision desktop users needing >2x), but moderate overstates a beyond-AA gap; minor.
